qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 provides for a ban on the export of plastic waste to non-OECD countries, including China, from 21 November 2026 until 21 May 2029 at the earliest. While the restriction is intended to prevent environmentally harmful waste management practices outside the EU, it may also affect recycling companies that are unable to find a sufficient number of buyers for specific material fractions in Europe. The inability to manage these materials in a cost-effective manner may lead to increased storage costs, reduced production or the closure of smaller facilities. In light of the above: 1.

Has the Commission carried out an impact assessment on how the ban will affect SMEs involved in plastics recycling, and does it have data on the European market’s capacity to manage material fractions previously exported outside the OECD?
What measures have been planned to ensure adequate infrastructure, demand and economic viability for the management of these materials within the EU?

Is the Commission considering transitional arrangements or other support mechanisms for businesses which, despite complying with environmental regulations, are unable to find buyers for the processed materials?
